newsitem.title: USA: Mass. $3 bln transportation bond bill moves ahead.
newsitem.headline: Mass. $3 bln transportation bond bill moves ahead.

text.p: The Massachusetts Transportation Committee approved a $3 billion, two-year borrowing package that allows the state to pay its massive Central Artery bills and provides money for road and bridge projects across the state.

The bill, passed late Wednesday, includes authorization for the state to borrow $1.3 billion over the next two years in anticipation of future federal revenues to pay bills on its share of the $10.7 billion Central Artery project, the nation's most expensive construction project to date.
Bills for the "Big Dig" are going to be paid out at a much higher rate than federal money will come in over the next few years.

These Grant Anticipation Notes are controversial because they are based on the gamble that the federal government will fund Massachusetts's transportation allotments at certain levels over the next five years. If it does not, the governor and legislature will have to identify new sources of revenue to pay off the notes.

The bill contains $150 million in direct transportation aid to cities and towns. It provides $2.2 billion in Central Artery costs and $504 million for road and bridge projects statewide, above and beyond the $150 million aid program.
The bill advanced on a voice vote. It will next be taken up by the House Committee on Long Term Debt.
The measure stipulates that the Massachusetts Turnpike Authority must pay $700 million worth of Central Artery costs. That writes into law a number that so far has been only a planning figure.
